title: Cost of a visit at San Francisco community health centers
question: What does one visit cost at the federally supported health centers based in San Francisco, and how has it moved?
finding: A cost per visit can be computed only for some centers in some years. Asian And Pacific Islander Wellness Center: $299 in 2022 and $698 in 2025 (+133%), as the money went from $4.1 million to $18.1 million (+339%) and the count from 13,766 to 25,923 (+88%). San Francisco Community Clinic Consortium: $329 in 2018 and $406 in 2020 (+24%), as the money went from $33.4 million to $37.9 million (+13%) and the count from 101,668 to 93,360 (-8%). Healthright 360: $465 in 2022 and $450 in 2024 (-3%), as the money went from $4.1 million to $5.9 million (+42%) and the count from 8,901 to 13,071 (+47%). Lyon-Martin Community Health Services: $584 in 2024 and $709 in 2025 (+21%), as the money went from $4.1 million to $8.9 million (+120%) and the count from 6,962 to 12,614 (+81%). Mission Neighborhood Health Center: $491 in 2024 and $506 in 2025 (+3%), as the money went from $34.5 million to $40.8 million (+18%) and the count from 70,192 to 80,575 (+15%).
how: Each health center in the federal Health Center Program files a yearly report in a standard form. For each San Francisco center and year in which the federal public file prints both figures, total cost after allocation of overhead (Table 8A) is divided by clinic and virtual visits (Table 5). The money is the center's whole cost from every payer, not City money. Each center is its own line; centers are not added together because the set with published figures changes from year to year.
limits: The federal public file withholds cost or visit figures for most centers in most years (for the rest of the Bay Area, both figures are printed for 7 of 23 centers in 2025 and 1 of 23 in 2021), so no citywide trend and no fair peer average can be built; a gap in a line is a year the figures were withheld. These reports are filed by the centers themselves under federal definitions and reviewed by the federal agency: a standard report, not an outside count. Centers serving homeless people or people with HIV have longer, costlier visits. A sharp change in one center's figure can come from a change in what the center reports as its own cost.
